metadata.note: Amtrak's own Pioneer -- not a 19th-century predecessor line, but a real Amtrak train (1977-1997) that Amtrak itself later discontinued. It was the last passenger rail service to serve Wyoming, southern Idaho, or eastern Oregon; no replacement has run this corridor since. Two eras, two geometries: 1977-1991 ran Seattle-Portland-Pendleton-Boise-Pocatello-Ogden-Salt Lake City (connecting at Ogden to the California Zephyr toward Chicago); from June 17 1991 it was rerouted to run its own through service to Denver and Chicago, branching east from Ogden through Wyoming on Union Pacific's Overland Route (Evanston-Green River-Rock Springs-Rawlins-Laramie-Cheyenne) to Denver rather than dipping south to Salt Lake City. East of Denver it combined with the existing Chicago-Denver route (already on this map as part of the modern California Zephyr in amtrak.geojson), so that shared segment isn't re-drawn here. The Seattle-Portland segment reuses the same real-traced geometry as southern_pacific_cascade.geojson. Three short stretches (Portland-The Dalles-Pendleton, and Ontario-Boise) could not be matched to a connected active-rail path in the time available and are straight-line approximations.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_(train) (launched June 7 1977, Seattle-Salt Lake City, connecting at Ogden with the San Francisco/California Zephyr; rerouted June 17 1991 via Union Pacific's Overland Route through Wyoming -- last used for passenger service in 1983 -- to Denver and Chicago; reduced to thrice-weekly Nov 4 1993; discontinued May 10 1997 when congressional funding mandate expired; last passenger rail to serve Wyoming, southern Idaho, or eastern Oregon)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for either era beyond the general daily/thrice-weekly cadence noted above.
geometry_sources: Seattle-Portland: reused from southern_pacific_cascade.geojson (already real-traced from OpenStreetMap)
Portland-Salt Lake City and Ogden-Denver: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API), railway=rail ways, for the corridor described above
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
